newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude prices flatten with trade thin.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude prices flatten with trade thin.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast crudes edged up late Thursday after a flat session which saw traders leaving the market to evaluate year-end inventories.
Traders were sidelined as oil companies squared their books and decided how much inventory should remain on hand at the end of the year.
"The traders don't have the foggiest notion whether they should go up or down," in inventory purchases, one buyer said.
Outright prices for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude ranged $20.35/20.65 a barrel, five cents over yesterday but flat from morning talk.
Discounts for ANS remained $2.30 in quiet trade, traders said.
A major producer said they offered crude at $2.10 but considered raising it.
Buyers said the producer's latest sale -- a partial cargo -- showed that ANS had fallen in value.
The 100,000 barrel parcel sold at $2.20 from off December West Texas Intermediate, but December WTI has fallen relative to November.
Buyers said they kept bids at a $2.50 discount.
Line 63 rose stayed five cents over Wednesday, with the range talked $19.55/19.85 a barrel.
Wilmington remained at $18.15/$18.25 a barrel, while Kern River crude stayed $16.65/$16.85 a barrel.
